Tiles of elevations from a grid

Source: R/tiles.R
rr_tiles_dem.Rd

A tile function for a dem or contour rr_layer() made from a grid of elevations: a GeoTIFF (a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF when it is large) or any grid GDAL reads, such as GEBCO's netCDF, in any projection; a terra SpatRaster; or a data frame of a grid's cells. Each tile the page asks for is warped from the grid by GDAL (through terra), the grid resampled once: averaged where a pixel is wider than a cell (the map zoomed out), interpolated (bilinear) where it is narrower. The tile is written as a PNG image in the Terrarium encoding, from which the page draws the relief, the colours and the contours, and fits them to the view.

Usage

rr_tiles_dem(
  x,
  lon = "lon",
  lat = "lat",
  elevation = "elevation",
  tile_size = 512L,
  minzoom = 0L,
  maxzoom = NULL,
  nodata = 0
)

Arguments

x

The grid: a path of a raster file, a terra SpatRaster, or a data frame (or a lazy table of at most 10 million rows, read into R) of a regular grid in longitude and latitude (WGS 84), a row per cell: its centre and its elevation. A cell may be missing, a row may not repeat a cell.

lon, lat, elevation

For a data frame, its columns: the centre's longitude and latitude, and the elevation in metres, negative below sea level (a depth is the elevation's negative: make the column first). For a raster of several layers, elevation names the one drawn; a raster's values are metres, negative below sea level.

tile_size

The tiles' side in pixels, 256 or 512.

minzoom, maxzoom

The zooms tiles are made for; the map draws deeper zooms from the deepest's tiles, enlarged. By default from 0 to the first zoom at which a pixel is no wider than a cell, but no deeper than 8: a pixel of about 300 m at the equator and 130 m at 65 degrees north (512-pixel tiles), an overview rather than every detail of a fine grid. Give maxzoom to go deeper; each zoom takes about four times the bytes of the one before.

nodata

The elevation written where the grid has none: beyond its edge, and where a cell a pixel is drawn from is missing. By default 0, sea level, which the colours of a depth leave clear.

Value

A function function(z, x, y) (y from the north, as the page asks) returning a tile's bytes, a PNG; a tile wholly outside the grid is level at nodata, for maplibre-contour draws no lines in a tile one of whose eight neighbours is missing. With the attributes rr_layer() takes for a dem or contour layer (format, encoding, tile_size, bounds, minzoom and maxzoom); source, by which rr_bundle() writes the tiles of layers on one grid once; count, the grid's number of cells, missing ones included; and fit, "page": a layer on these tiles fits its colours, contours and shading to the view in the page, from the tiles in view, with no call to R (the rules of rr_bundle()'s fit, by default the floor and the cap at the 2nd and 98th percentiles of the values in view, 25 quantiles between them, and the shading's intensity 2 over the 90th percentile of the slope in degrees, between 0.3 and 1).

Details

A grid is read where it is: only the part under a tile, and from a GeoTIFF's overviews where a pixel spans eight cells or more (the full grid nearer the deepest zoom, as overviews average twice). A large grid that is no Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF is read whole for a tile zoomed far out: gdal_translate -of COG makes one, losing nothing.

See also

rr_tiles_mbtiles(), for tiles already made; rr_layer()

Examples

# a small hill, 21 by 21 cells of 0.01 degrees
g <- expand.grid(lon = seq(10, 10.2, by = 0.01), lat = seq(56, 56.2, by = 0.01))
g$elevation <- 100 - 5000 * ((g$lon - 10.1)^2 + (g$lat - 56.1)^2)
if (requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  tiles <- rr_tiles_dem(g)
  attributes(tiles)[c("bounds", "minzoom", "maxzoom", "count")]
  png_bytes <- tiles(10, 540, 318) # the tile over the hill at zoom 10
  rgb <- png::readPNG(png_bytes) * 255
  # the Terrarium encoding: (red * 256 + green + blue / 256) - 32768
  range(rgb[, , 1] * 256 + rgb[, , 2] + rgb[, , 3] / 256 - 32768)

  # the same grid as a GeoTIFF, as most grids come
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
  terra::writeRaster(terra::rast(g, type = "xyz", crs = "EPSG:4326"), f)
  attributes(rr_tiles_dem(f))[c("bounds", "maxzoom")]
}
#> $bounds
#> [1]  9.995 55.995 10.205 56.205
#> 
#> $maxzoom
#> [1] 7
#>
